title: Portrayal rack file (v4)
description: A Rack Builder document: one or more racks, the devices in them, and the cables between their ports. What the kit's Rack Builder reads and writes.

version.description: The file version. Older files are migrated on load; newer ones are refused. Version 4 carries half-unit positions and the keys of the rack file version 4 design note. A reader keeps a key it does not know, at every level of the file.

id.description: The document's id, unique in a browser's library.

racks.description: The racks. The Rack Builder edits the first.

items.description: Devices and cable managers on the rails.

zeroU.description: Parts that stand beside the rack at an attachment point and take no rack unit, such as vertical cable managers. An entry with an id, a ref and an attachment point is placed; any other entry is kept as written.

dcim.description: Names a NetBox or Nautobot import needs. Present only once set; unknown fields are kept.

bundles.description: Cable bundles: cables combed into one run and strapped. Optional; a rack with none may leave it out.

numbering.description: Which way the U labels count. Positions are always stored bottom-up.

thread.description: The thread of tapped holes; null for square.

railDepth.description: Millimetres between front and rear rails; null on two posts.

usableDepth.description: Millimetres from the front rail to the deepest point a device may reach.

ref.description: A catalogue rack this frame was taken from, if any.

startU.description: The number of the first unit, for a frame whose labels do not start at 1. Absent is 1.

setback.description: Millimetres a faceplate stands behind its rail in this rack, for an item that states none of its own. Absent until set.

width.description: The rail width in inches. Absent is 19.

options.description: The options of a catalogue rack this frame takes. Kept as written; nothing reads one until a product defines it.

id.description: Unique within the rack, and never reused while a cable end names it.

ref.description: The device, by its catalogue ref.

label.description: The name shown on the drawing.

ru.description: Its bottom, in rack units counted bottom-up from 1, in steps of 0.5: 12 is the bottom of U12 and 12.5 the middle of it.

face.description: The face it is mounted on.

swaps.description: What the Explorer seated: slot path to part ref.

on.description: A cable manager's host: the id of the device it bolts over.

unit.description: Which of the host's units, from 1 at its bottom.

side.description: left or right: the rail a part narrower than the rack opening is on, seen from its face. Absent, it is across both rails.

roll.description: Degrees it is rolled clockwise, as seen in the elevation of the face it is on. Absent is upright.

readingsAsWritten.description: Readings the loader could not use, kept whole as they were written.

setback.description: Millimetres its faceplate stands behind its rail. Absent, the device default and then the frame setback apply.

heldBy.description: What holds an item that is not bolted to the rails itself: a shelf, a drawer or a rail of another item.

item.description: The id of the item that holds it.

at.description: Which place on that item, by its id there.

turn.description: How it is turned on that place.

zeroU.description: A part beside the rack. Its place (id, ref, at, offsetMm) is described but not constrained, so an entry of another shape is still a valid entry; the kit places an entry whose id, ref and at are non-empty strings, and keeps any other as written. What it is set to (swaps, fields, states, readings, heldBy) is typed as on an item.

id.description: Unique within the rack's zeroU entries; z1, z2 and so on. The loader gives an entry without one an id.

ref.description: The part, by its catalogue ref.

label.description: The name shown on the drawing.

at.description: The attachment point it stands at: left or right on a two-post, left-front, right-front, left-rear or right-rear on a four-post. The lane of that name runs beside it.

offsetMm.description: A number: its bottom, in millimetres above the bottom of the rails; a whole number of U as the kit writes it.

between.description: True when it stands between this rack and the next one, serving both.

swaps.description: What is seated in it: slot path to part ref, as on an item.

fields.description: Its part settings, as on an item.

heldBy.description: What it hangs on, such as the two brackets of a PDU.

parts.description: The ids of the zero-U entries of this rack that hold it, one or more.

channel.description: The channel of the frame it stands in, by its id on the catalogue rack the frame names.

readingsAsWritten.description: Readings the loader could not use, kept whole as they were written.

item.description: The device's id. A removed device's id is kept, and the end reads as loose.

path.description: The port's path on the face. A power inlet, an outlet, a DC terminal or a ground stud is named by the path of its connector slot.

view.description: Which of the device's own panels the port is on.

plug.description: The plug or lug the cable has at this end, as a component ref. Stated only where the port takes more than one; absent, the plug is derived from what the port accepts.

waypoint.description: One stop on a route: an element of a placed device's drawing (item and via), or a lane beside the rails at a U (lane and ru).

item.description: A placed device's id, with via.

via.description: The element of that device's drawing the cable passes through, such as a ring or a duct.

lane.description: A lane beside the rails, with ru.

ru.description: The U the lane is crossed at.

media.description: The cable type (os2, om3, om4, om5, cat6, cat6a, dac, aoc, power, ground, stack, usb, console), or empty. power is a conductor that carries power, an AC cord or a DC feed, and the cable of a redundant or stacked power link; ground is a bonding conductor; stack joins the stacking ports of two switches; usb is a USB link; console is a console link. A reader that does not know a value keeps it.

unit.description: As written; m when the file stated none.

source.description: Where it came from: entered, or routed when the Rack Builder worked it out from the route.

measured.description: Written before version 4: metres along the route with the allowances of then. A version-4 kit writes need in its place and drops this at the next measure.

need.description: Metres the cable must at least be: its path, what is inside its two ports and the short tolerance of its maker. Present beside a routed length.

lengthAsWritten.description: A length the loader could not use, kept whole as it was written.

color.description: The cable's own color: # and six lower-case hex digits. Absent, the jacket color of its two ends (when both state one and they agree), else its type's, else its media's is drawn.

colorAsWritten.description: A color the loader could not use, kept whole as it was written. The cable then has no color of its own.

route.description: The waypoints the cable runs through, in order. Empty means the Rack Builder chooses the way.

routeEdited.description: True once someone has changed the route by hand, so it is no longer chosen for them.

routeAsWritten.description: A route containing an entry the loader could not read, kept whole as it was written. The readable waypoints are in route.

slack.description: Where the spare length is stored. Absent, nothing has been said; an empty list says it is stored nowhere.

slackAsWritten.description: A slack list holding an entry the loader could not use, kept whole as it was written. The usable entries are in slack.

lay.description: Where the cable was laid by hand in a pathway.

straps.description: The straps of a single cable.

anchors.description: False for no strap tying it to a tray it passes.

bundle.description: Cables sharing part of their route, combed into one run and held with hook-and-loop straps. Membership is here only: a cable carries no bundle key.

id.description: b1, b2 and so on: unique within the rack, and not the id of an item, a part beside the rack or a cable.

number.description: Unique within the rack. What a tag prints when there is no label.

label.description: The bundle's name; empty for Bundle <number>.

members.description: The cables, in combing order. A cable is in at most one bundle.

route.description: The trunk: the run the members share, as waypoints in order.

routeAsWritten.description: A trunk containing an entry the loader could not read, kept whole as it was written. The readable waypoints are in route.

straps.description: The hook-and-loop straps. Absent means every 12 in, with breakout and anchor straps.

breakout.description: Whether a strap goes beside each point where a cable joins or leaves the bundle. When left out: true, unless every is null.

anchors.description: Whether the bundle is strapped to each tray with tie slots it lies on. When left out: true, unless every is null.

a.description: The trunk waypoint where it leaves the bundle for its a end. Absent, it joins where its own route first meets the trunk.

b.description: The trunk waypoint where it leaves the bundle for its b end. Absent, it leaves where its own route last meets the trunk.

strapSpacing.description: How far apart the spacing straps are, a length with its own unit; null for none.

states.description: What each switchable part is set to: part path to state name.

readings.description: Readings taken from the device, with where they came from and when.

at.description: When they were taken, as an RFC 3339 time.

values.description: Part path to what was read there.

additionalProperties.description: What was read at one part.

slackEntry.description: Spare stored in a tray or on a spool of a placed part (item and via), or left at one end of the cable (end). At most one entry of a cable has no value: it takes the rest.

item.description: The id of the placed item or zero-U part, with via.

via.description: The tray or spool on that part, with item.

end.description: The end of the cable the spare is left at.

form.description: How it is stored; a coil when left out.

unit.description: The unit of value; m when left out.

layEntry.description: One pathway the cable was laid in by hand. An entry states a position, a face, or both.

item.description: The id of the placed part the pathway is on.

position.description: Its place across the pathway, counted from 1.

face.description: The face of a tray it lies on.
